newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money slips after Buba injects funds.
newsitem.headline: German call money slips after Buba injects funds.

text.p: German call money rates nudged slightly lower in Wednesday trade after the Bundesbank injected a net 3.5 billion marks in new funds at this week's tender award.

Dealers said call money rates were trading between 3.05/07 percent on Wednesday compared with rates of 3.05/10 percent on Tuesday, when the market had expected the central bank to largely replace funds expiring on Wednesday.
While the Bundesbank kept its key money market rate, the repo, steady at three percent, the central bank did replace the expiring 82.4 billion mark pact with an 85.9 billion mark pact.
Dealers said the award was more generous than expected but added that the funds would likely be needed by the market.
Reserve data, calculated on Wednesday morning, indicated that the market would need a touch more money this week.
Banks' daily reserve holdings slipped to 38.7 billion marks on Tuesday from 40.3 billion marks on Monday, leaving the monthly average holdings to slip to 39.9 billion marks from 40.2 billion marks.
Banks borrowed 300 million marks of funds at the 4.50 percent emergency borrowing rate.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average (FIONA) was set at 3.09300 percent on Wednesday compared with 3.10567 percent on Tuesday.
